guide_enrichment.narrative: Our view starts with how closely the market matches our broader expectation. Maryland has produced encouraging early results, but we do not see a meaningful pricing disagreement to exploit here. The Terrapins held UConn to 67 rushing yards and recorded five sacks, yet our efficiency numbers still identify Nebraska’s ground game against Maryland’s run defense as the most significant mismatch.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: For us, the matchup to watch is Nebraska’s rushing offense against Maryland’s defensive front. Maryland’s performance against UConn was impressive, but one result does not outweigh the larger efficiency profile. If Nebraska consistently creates manageable downs on the ground, Maryland will need its passing game to answer against a more challenging defensive matchup than the early production might suggest. That tension supports the market’s current position and leaves us without enough value to get involved.

guide_extractions.document_match_reason: The guide is for Maryland's Sept. 19, 2026 home game against Virginia Tech, identified as Game 3. Maryland's schedule lists the Nebraska game for Oct. 3, 2026, after the Sept. 26 UCLA game.

recent_game.fact: Maryland improved to 2-0 with a 38-14 road win over UConn on Sept. 12, producing 475 total yards and 27 first downs.
Maryland rushed for 125 yards and three touchdowns against UConn while completing 35 of 42 passes for 350 yards.
Maryland held UConn to 223 total yards, including 67 rushing yards, and recorded five sacks.
Maryland had two second-quarter scoring drives of at least 90 yards against UConn, its first game with multiple 90-yard drives since 2018.

quarterback.fact: Starting quarterback Malik Washington completed 34 of 41 passes for 347 yards and two touchdowns against UConn, including a program-record 18 consecutive completions.
Through two games in 2026, Washington had completed 53 of 72 passes for 533 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions.
Washington started all 12 games as a true freshman in 2025 and passed for 2,963 yards and 17 touchdowns.
Transfer quarterback Cardell Williams is the experienced reserve; he started the final 10 games for Sacramento State in 2025 and completed 111 of 176 passes for 1,651 yards and 10 touchdowns.

offensive_personnel.fact: Maryland's offensive line against UConn consisted of left tackle Rahtrel Perry, left guard Amory Hills, center Michael Hershey, right guard Ryan Howerton and right tackle Isaiah Wright; the unit blocked for 475 total yards.
Amory Hills made his first Maryland start at left guard against UConn after transfer Tellek Lockette started the opener there.
Left tackle Rahtrel Perry entered the guide with a team-high 39 career starts and 39 consecutive starts.

Transfer receivers Na'eem Abdul-Rahim Gladding and Chris Durr Jr. both exceeded 100 receiving yards against UConn: Gladding had eight catches for 130 yards and a touchdown, while Durr had 10 catches for 106 yards and a touchdown.
Through two games, Gladding had 14 receptions for 187 yards and two touchdowns, while Durr had 16 receptions for 147 yards and one touchdown.
Running back Iverson Howard had 26 carries for 121 yards and three touchdowns through two games.
USC transfer Harry Dalton III rushed for 48 yards and two touchdowns against UConn and scored a rushing touchdown in each of Maryland's first two games.

defensive_personnel.fact: Sidney Stewart recorded six tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, one sack and a forced fumble against UConn.
DD Holmes led Maryland with 2.5 sacks through two games; Eyan Thomas and UCF transfer Derrick LeBlanc each had two sacks.
Freshman linebacker Zion Elee recorded his first career sack and forced a fumble against UConn; DD Holmes recovered the fumble.
Maryland added defensive linemen Lavon Johnson from Texas, Derrick LeBlanc from UCF, and Armon and Jayvon Parker from Washington through the transfer portal.
West Virginia transfer Jordan Scruggs and Boston College transfer Amari Jackson were among Maryland's starting defensive backs against UConn.

coaching_changes.fact: Clint Trickett became Maryland's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach after serving as Jacksonville State's offensive coordinator in 2025.
Matt Barnes returned to Maryland as special teams coordinator after two seasons as Mississippi State's co-defensive coordinator and safeties coach.
Randy Starks became Maryland's defensive line coach, and Kyle Schmitt took over the tight ends room.

offensive_context.fact: Through two games, Maryland averaged 560.5 total yards, 315.5 passing yards, 245 rushing yards and 50 points per game.
Maryland converted 55.2 percent of its third downs through two games.
Maryland scored nine rushing touchdowns in its first two games.
Maryland committed no turnovers in either of its first two games.

defensive_context.fact: Maryland recorded 10 sacks in its first two games, the most in the Big Ten and tied for fourth nationally at the time of the guide.
Through two games, Maryland allowed 154 total yards, 38.5 rushing yards, 115.5 passing yards and seven points per game.
Maryland held 18 consecutive opponents below 300 passing yards entering the Virginia Tech game.
Opponents converted 26.9 percent of their third downs through Maryland's first two games.

special_teams.fact: Kicker Sean O'Haire made field goals from 19 yards against UConn and from 26 and 36 yards against Hampton.
Na'eem Abdul-Rahim Gladding averaged 17 yards on two punt returns through two games, with a long return of 34 yards.
